pr_title: Ensure converter factories do not throw on unsupported types.
pr_body:
This PR:

* Updates the Enumerable and FSharp converter factories so that they don't throw exceptions at converter construction time when encountering unsupported types. They instead produce `UnsupportedTypeConverter<T>` instances, consistent with how we handle unsupported types elsewhere. This makes it possible to materialize metadata for unsupported types, fixing #80914.
* Adds detection for multi-dimensional arrays in the source generator, which also produces `UnsupportedTypeConverter<T>`, ensuring consistency with the reflection serializer and how other unsupported types are handled.
* Makes minor updates to the assertions of the unsupported type test suite, which were until now relying on the fact that the converter factory itself was throwing for multi-dimensional arrays.

Fix #80914.

issue_context.title: Regression with JsonConverter attribute with System.Text.Json 7
comments:
Tagging subscribers to this area: @dotnet/area-system-text-json, @gregsdennis See info in [area-owners.md](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/main/docs/area-owners.md) if you want to be subscribed.
Issue Details
### Description When upgrading `System.Text.Json` from version 6.0.7 to 7.0.1 in an application targeting .NET 6 we experienced a `NotSupportedException` in code that worked fine before the upgrade. This particular code uses a custom `JsonConverter` to serialize a `Double[,]`array. ### Reproduction Steps The following small project fails with a `NotSupportedException` when trying to serialize the DTO. *.csproj file: ```xml Exe net6.0 enable enable ``` Program.cs: ```csharp using System.Text.Json; using System.Text.Json.Serialization; using systemtextjson7regression; var dto = new Dto() { Data = new double[,] { { 1, 243 }, { 1, 2 } } }; JsonSerializer.SerializeToUtf8Bytes(dto); namespace systemtextjson7regression { public class DoubleMatrixJsonConverter : JsonConverter { /// public override double[,] Read(ref Utf8JsonReader reader, Type typeToConvert, JsonSerializerOptions options) => throw new NotImplementedException(); /// public override void Write(Utf8JsonWriter writer, double[,] value, JsonSerializerOptions options) { } } class Dto { [JsonConverter(typeof(DoubleMatrixJsonConverter))] public double[,] Data { get; set; } } } ``` ### Expected behavior The programme terminates without throwing an exception: ``` Unhandled exception. System.NotSupportedException: The type 'System.Double[,]' is not supported. at System.Text.Json.ThrowHelper.ThrowNotSupportedException_SerializationNotSupported(Type propertyType) at System.Text.Json.Serialization.Converters.IEnumerableConverterFactory.CreateConverter(Type typeToConvert, JsonSerializerOptions options) at System.Text.Json.Serialization.JsonConverterFactory.GetConverterInternal(Type typeToConvert, JsonSerializerOptions options) at System.Text.Json.Serialization.Metadata.DefaultJsonTypeInfoResolver.GetConverterForType(Type typeToConvert, JsonSerializerOptions options, Boolean resolveJsonConverterAttribute) at System.Text.Json.Serialization.Metadata.DefaultJsonTypeInfoResolver.CreateJsonTypeInfo(Type type, JsonSerializerOptions options) at System.Text.Json.Serialization.Metadata.DefaultJsonTypeInfoResolver.GetTypeInfo(Type type, JsonSerializerOptions options) at System.Text.Json.JsonSerializerOptions.GetTypeInfoNoCaching(Type type) at System.Collections.Concurrent.ConcurrentDictionary`2.GetOrAdd(TKey key, Func`2 valueFactory) at System.Text.Json.JsonSerializerOptions.GetTypeInfoInternal(Type type, Boolean ensureConfigured, Boolean resolveIfMutable) at System.Text.Json.Serialization.Metadata.JsonPropertyInfo.Configure() at System.Text.Json.Serialization.Metadata.JsonTypeInfo.InitializePropertyCache() at System.Text.Json.Serialization.Metadata.JsonTypeInfo.Configure() at System.Text.Json.Serialization.Metadata.JsonTypeInfo.g__ConfigureLocked|143_0() at System.Text.Json.JsonSerializerOptions.GetTypeInfoInternal(Type type, Boolean ensureConfigured, Boolean resolveIfMutable) at System.Text.Json.JsonSerializer.GetTypeInfo(JsonSerializerOptions options, Type inputType) at System.Text.Json.JsonSerializer.GetTypeInfo[T](JsonSerializerOptions options) at System.Text.Json.JsonSerializer.SerializeToUtf8Bytes[TValue](TValue value, JsonSerializerOptions options) at Program.
$(String[] args) in C:\Users\Morten Boysen\source\repos\systemtextjson7regression\systemtextjson7regression\Program.cs:line 6 ``` ### Actual behavior A `NotSupportedException` is thrown. ### Regression? Yes, this worked on .NET 6 with `System.Net.Json` version 6.0.7. An interesting observation is that this fails with both version 6.0.7 and 7.0.1 of `System.Text.Json` iff the target framework is .NET 7. That means the error matrix looks like this: Target framwork .NET 6 and `System.Net.Json` version 6.0.7: Works Target framwork .NET 7 and `System.Net.Json` version 7.0.1: Fails Target framwork .NET 7 and `System.Net.Json` version 6.0.7: Fails Target framwork .NET 7 and `System.Net.Json` version 7.0.1: Fails ### Known Workarounds Explicitly adding the converter to the converter collection makes the code work on all target platform/`System.Text.Json` combinations: ```csharp using System.Text.Json; using System.Text.Json.Serialization; using systemtextjson7regression; var dto = new Dto() { Data = new double[,] { { 1, 243 }, { 1, 2 } } }; var options = new JsonSerializerOptions(); options.Converters.Add(new DoubleMatrixJsonConverter()); JsonSerializer.SerializeToUtf8Bytes(dto, options); namespace systemtextjson7regression { public class DoubleMatrixJsonConverter : JsonConverter { /// public override double[,] Read(ref Utf8JsonReader reader, Type typeToConvert, JsonSerializerOptions options) => throw new NotImplementedException(); /// public override void Write(Utf8JsonWriter writer, double[,] value, JsonSerializerOptions options) { } } class Dto { //[JsonConverter(typeof(DoubleMatrixJsonConverter))] public double[,] Data { get; set; } } } ``` However, this does not work in our scenario, as the assembly defining the DTO and custom converter is not referenced by the assembly creating the serializer and doing the serialization, so we cannot register the converter (the two assemblies are both being referenced by a third assembly, creating the application). ### Configuration This fails on Windows 10 and 11. ### Other information _No response_

I can reproduce. The issue is caused by the fact that we're now eagerly resolving the default converter for the type:

https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/a734aa467f1bbf4d5bf30fe217e1a36eb966ce08/src/libraries/System.Text.Json/src/System/Text/Json/Serialization/Metadata/DefaultJsonTypeInfoResolver.cs#L84-L107

which in the case of multi-dimensional arrays is throwing an exception:

https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/a734aa467f1bbf4d5bf30fe217e1a36eb966ce08/src/libraries/System.Text.Json/src/System/Text/Json/Serialization/Converters/Collection/IEnumerableConverterFactory.cs#L43-L53

We should change the built-in converter factory so that instead of throwing it returns an instance of `UnsupportedTypeConverter` like we already do with other unsupported types:

https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/a734aa467f1bbf4d5bf30fe217e1a36eb966ce08/src/libraries/System.Text.Json/src/System/Text/Json/Serialization/Converters/Value/UnsupportedTypeConverter.cs#L6-L13

We should audit the remaining built-in converter factories for cases where we currently throw at construction time.

Just out of my curiosity, why does this fail on .NET 7, when the package reference for `System.Text.Json` is explicitly set to 6.0.7? Is the runtime somehow choosing a version 7 package of System.Text.Json anyway on .NET 7?
IIRC it is not possible to reference versions of STJ earlier than the one available in the shared framework.

review_comments: I think we should open the issue and try to support the multidimensional dictionaries

I checked the backlog and there doesn't appear to be a request for that so far. I think we should leave it up to the users to pick a JSON representation that suites their requirements (for example, a jagged array would work for most cases, but it might not be the most compact representation when needing to marshal matrices).
can we add same test with custom converter added through options?
I don't think custom converters are in scope for this particular test suite or this change. We have a separate test suite tracking custom converters and how they handle null values.
it might make sense to `??=` here and remove `readonly` from `_errorMessage`
It's intentional. I wouldn't want the converter to root additional memory just to optimize throwing exceptions.
